newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling strengthens against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling strengthens against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened against the dollar on Thursday as export sales continued to flow into the market, traders said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 55.97 against the dollar from 56.03 on Wednesday. Against the pound, the shilling was posted at an average of 87.66 from 87.71 on Wednesday.
"Heavy exporter sales into the market piled pressure on the dollar as trade was briefly carried out under the 56 level," a dealer said.
A banker said a number of institutions were seen off-loading foreign exchange in favour of a stronger shilling attracting high interest rates.

"The market opened at 56.00/12 before dipping to close at 55.90/05. The central bank is still supporting the greenback as exporters feel the pinch of a weaker dollar. They intervened and sold shillings at 56.03 levels," the dealer said.
Dealers said overnight money market rates slid further down to 10-15 percent levels.
